title: 5th Sitting of first Session of 2025
summary: The 5th sitting opened with the day's agenda and a committee sitting notice, and the chair sent five non-resident ambassador nominations to the Foreign Relations committee. Members then debated committee reports on the President's nominees for Elections Commission president and vice president, Anti-Corruption Commission vice president, and Minister of Tourism and Environment. Some members questioned how independent the appointment process is and raised corruption concerns, while others backed the nominees and the process. After a recess, all four nominees were approved with 68-69 yes votes and none against, and the sitting ended at 11:14 with the next sitting set for 18 February.

items.title: Committee report on appointing the Elections Commission president and vice president

items.title: Committee report on appointing the Anti-Corruption Commission vice president
Committee report on approving the Minister of Tourism and Environment
Putting pending matters to a vote
items.outcome: four votes held after a recess (09:52 to 11:00) and a short pause for a voting-system problem; all passed

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Backed the nominees and urged quick approval; said the committee includes members of every party.
Said the Majlis, not the President, decides appointments; objected that debate had drifted from the report.
Described the Anti-Corruption Commission as important and criticised past-government procurement, asking it to look into them.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Criticised the constitutional change giving the President a larger role in appointments, noting a pending Supreme Court case.
Raised corruption concerns in state institutions and said some complaints are not investigated.
On the tourism minister: asked for more jobs and benefits for Maldivians and attention to environmental harm.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Said MDA was given no seat on the committee that reviewed the nominees.
Supported the nominee but criticised the Anti-Corruption Commission's record on several cases.
Backed the tourism minister nominee; complained the finance minister does not answer MPs' calls.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Voiced concern that the appointment changes weaken the independence of independent institutions.
Raised the Elections Commission and the use of personal data to enrol people in a party.
Said independent bodies lack the freedom to act and that the process leaves members unable to judge outcomes.

speakers.name: Hussain Riza Adam
positions: Presented the Independent Institutions committee's reports on the Elections Commission and Anti-Corruption Commission nominees.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Made a short remark about the Anti-Corruption Commission in a point of order the chair did not accept.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Raised a point of order about speakers staying on the report; the chair did not accept it as one.

speakers.name: Qasim Ibrahim
positions: Supported the report and the amendment, saying the Majlis still decides by vote on the President's nominees.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Said the Majlis decides appointments by member vote, not the President.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Said a party was speaking on the report without studying it; the chair did not accept it as a point of order.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Presented the government accountability committee's report on the Tourism and Environment minister nominee.

speakers.name: Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the tourism and environment nominee and backed the government's reform steps.

decisions: Five non-resident ambassador nominations were referred to the Foreign Relations committee.
Mohamed Zahid approved as Elections Commission president (68 yes, 0 no).
Abdul Rahman Salah Rasheed approved as Elections Commission vice president (69 yes, 0 no).
Abdulla Nashid approved as Anti-Corruption Commission vice president (69 yes, 0 no).
Thoriq Ibrahim approved as Minister of Tourism and Environment (69 yes, 0 no).
Next sitting set for Tuesday 18 February 2025 at 9:00.
